key_gap: vs baseline: the v5 human baseline's home-turf moves — constraint-to-principle conversion ('the only thing that pulls is the rubber band'), the iterative tightening pass, band pre-tension, exact budget discipline — are now produced first-class by the routed m030 pass (hard/soft classification FIRST, deliberate severe-constraint solution, constraint-compatibility check on output, constraint-augmentation iteration), closing the v5 AI's admitted gap (it complied but never tightened) and flipping the verdict from human 4.6/4.4 to AI 4.9/4.6. The m003 inversion gate adds 6 ranked failure categories and the m007 ruin screen adds a probe-gated floor (100 g step) the baseline asserted away. Residual gap: physical capacity stays ±50% (unmeasured material properties) until the 3-step test runs — the design is APPROXIMATED, not SOLVED; the baseline's asserted margin is never tested either, so this is a shared, not a losing, gap.
learning_signal: On severe-constraint design tasks the winning move is not compliance — it is treating the constraint list as a generative operator and then iteratively tightening it: inventory constraints, convert each into a design principle (no cutting → joints are load-bearing; bending unavailable → axial-only; only the band pulls → band lashings), kill the naive candidate on numbers (deck ≈ 40–80 g < 200 g), then re-impose stricter self-constraints (every kit element earns its role, tape caps, exact symmetry) and re-run once. Comply-and-stop produces sound but unrefined designs; the tightening iteration is where margin and elegance come from.
suggested_improvement: Make the m030 contract (hard/soft classification FIRST + deliberate severe-constraint solution + constraint-compatibility check on the output) a standing pass for design signatures with a binding kit list, and move the constraint-augmentation iteration (>=2 stricter self-constraints forcing >=1 refinement) inside the pass so tightening happens in the contract, not as a REVIEW afterthought; pair with the m003 inversion gate so failure structure (joint peel, buckling, sway) is derived before the spec is fixed, and keep the 3-step load protocol as the packet's arbiter for ±50% physical estimates.

key_gap: vs baseline: the pure-style baseline fell into constraint-worship exactly as the registry predicts (rule = fixed context; beautiful 5,000-LOC stdlib stack; explicit refusal to question the rule), while the v6 route holds the trap style out of top-3 (the learned NEG lesson is installed), dual-routes m063 (multi-party: the approved dependency list is a standing exception, waiver is pre-approved) and m064 (the conflict dissolves on the cost table — pin + re-audit preserves the audit intent), and runs the P5 hard/soft screen FIRST with compliance priced (6 person-months + hand-rolled auth) vs removal (2 days + one waiver) against the binding deadline. Residual gap: the dual-route synthesis costs one reconciliation step the decision itself does not need (all passes agree), and the C' fallback's auth path still depends on a security sign-off if the waiver were denied — detect-and-escalate, not resolved.
learning_signal: An owned, waivable, outdated rule is a parameter to test, not a fence: classify constraints hard vs soft FIRST (origin, owner, waiver path, cost of compliance vs cost of removal), and when removal dominates, escalate the waiver and replace the blunt rule with a precise one (one pinned, audited, vendored dependency; re-audit on CVE) that preserves the original intent. 'Creative within the rule' is how constraint-worship manufactures elaborate wrongness; on deadline signatures the ruin screen must compare floors — ship on deadline with audited auth vs a 100%-capacity custom stack with a hand-rolled auth tail.
suggested_improvement: Keep the learned routing that holds m030 out of top-3 on decide/high_stakes signatures with a policy rule present; install the P5 hard/soft constraint screen plus an owner/waiver audit (origin, owner, waiver path, compliance-vs-removal cost table required before HOW) as a WHAT gate for any signature containing a stated 'non-negotiable' rule; and extend the m007 ruin screen on deadline+high_stakes signatures to always price the denied-request fallback branch with a named floor deliverable.
